paper.paper_scope: Experimentally investigates how Al content (15, 17, 19 at.%) affects the aging hardening behavior of Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%) low-density steels, focusing on β-Mn precipitation kinetics, intrinsic hardness of β-Mn, achievable hardness range, specific hardness, and fracture toughness over aging at 525-650 °C for 1-10 h.
paper.title: Effects of Al contents on aging hardening behaviors of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with ultra-high specific hardness

processes.description: Ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h, hot-rolled into 4 mm plates, then solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon and oil quenched; a single α (BCC) phase soft state with hardness ~253.4 (15Al), 259.8 (17Al) and 263.8 (19Al) HV.

processes.processes_notes: Identical solution treatment applied to all three alloys (15Al, 17Al, 19Al); this state is the parent of all aging treatments. Preceded by homogenization (1200 °C/24 h) and hot rolling, which are not separately modeled as process entities.

unmapped_findings: Achievable hardness range across the three Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels spanned 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV through simple aging treatments (b0037).
Peak hardness values: 965.6 HV for 15Al (600 °C/6 h), 924.9 HV for 17Al (575 °C/6 h), 917.8 HV for 19Al (600 °C/10 h); these values were used for fracture toughness tests (b0021, b0038).
Fracture toughness KIC of the hardest samples: 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 (15Al), 6.6 MPa·m^1/2 (17Al), 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 (19Al), decreasing with increasing Al content (b0061).

Nanoindentation microhardness of hardest samples: 11.7±0.4 GPa (15Al), 11.1±0.6 GPa (17Al), 10.4±1.3 GPa (19Al); intrinsic hardness of β-Mn: 12.1±0.3 GPa (15Al), 12.2±0.1 GPa (17Al), 12.5±0.4 GPa (19Al) (b0060).
Al content of β-Mn in the hardest samples (SEM-EDS): 14.3 at.% (15Al), 16.3 at.% (17Al), 17.5 at.% (19Al) (b0060).
Elastic moduli measured from compressive stress-strain curves: 164 GPa (15Al), 175 GPa (17Al), 181 GPa (19Al) (b0023).
Ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g achieved in the Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu low-density steel due to ultra-high hardness and low density (b0008, b0077).
Densities measured by Archimedes method: 6.85 g·cm⁻³ (15Al), 6.76 g·cm⁻³ (17Al), 6.66 g·cm⁻³ (19Al) (b0017).
Aging-induced phase evolution sequence: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (b0068).

Reference alloys discussed from previous/literature work but NOT studied in this paper: Fe-34Mn-10Al-0.76C (b0010), Fe-31Mn-11Al-0.89C (b0011), prior Fe-37.8Mn-6.9Al and Fe-36.5Mn-6.5Al-7.7Cu (wt.%) (b0065).
